polymers.introduction: Polymers are macromolecules built from repeating monomers. Degree of polymerization n up to 10⁵, molar mass thousands to millions. Properties depend on monomer, tacticity, crosslinking, and crystallinity. Two families: addition (chain-growth) and condensation (step-growth).

classification.mechanism: Initiation → Propagation (radical/cationic/anionic or coordination) → Termination. Monomers contain C=C (vinyl) or strained ring. No small molecule lost: monomer → polymer. Active center adds monomer sequentially.

examples.variants: LDPE (branched, film) vs HDPE (linear, bottle); catalyst: Ziegler-Natta (TiCl4/AlEt3) gives stereoregular

examples.tacticity: Isotactic (all CH3 same side, crystalline) via Ziegler-Natta; atactic (random) amorphous

examples.uses: Pipes, cables, flooring; plasticized with phthalates

examples.polymer: Polyacrylonitrile (PAN, acrylic fiber) → carbon fiber precursor

classification.initiators: Benzoyl peroxide (radical), BF3 (cationic for isobutylene), BuLi (anionic for styrene)

classification.mechanism: Monomers with two functional groups react stepwise, releasing small molecule (H2O, HCl, MeOH). Each step is independent; dimer → trimer → oligomer → polymer. Carothers equation: p = extent, DP = 1/(1-p); need p>0.99 for high DP. No active center.

examples.uses: Fibers, stockings, parachutes; hydrogen bonding gives high strength

examples.notes: Ring-opening is addition-like but chemically condensation family

examples.uses: Foams, coatings; blowing agent gives flexible/rigid foams
Electrical insulators, adhesive; first synthetic polymer (1907)
Rubber, sealants, breast implants; Si-O flexibility

thermoplasticVsThermoset.thermoplastic: Linear or branched, no crosslinks; melts on heating (reprocessable): PE, PP, PS, PVC, PET, nylon. Crystalline regions give strength; amorphous give transparency.
thermoplasticVsThermoset.thermoset: Cross-linked network (covalent between chains) formed on curing; does NOT melt (degrades on heating): epoxy, Bakelite, vulcanized rubber (S bridges), polyurethane network. Strong, heat resistant.
thermoplasticVsThermoset.elastomer: Lightly cross-linked + flexible chains (Tg below room T) → reversible stretch: vulcanized cis-polyisoprene (natural rubber + S), SBR, silicone rubber.

propertiesAndTuning: Tg (glass transition): below Tg = glassy brittle; above Tg = rubbery. Tg ↑ with rigidity, aromatic, H-bonding. PE Tg -80°C (flexible at RT), PS Tg 100°C (rigid).
Crystallinity: ordered packing ↑ strength, mp, density. Isotactic PP crystalline; atactic amorphous.
Plasticizer: lowers Tg (PVC rigid→flexible with phthalates).
Biodegradable: PLA (poly(lactic acid) from corn) –[O-CH(CH3)-CO]n–, PHB bacterial polyester, starch-based; hydrolyze via ester.
polymers.environment: Problems: persistence (PE ~500 yr), microplastics. Solutions: recycling codes (1 PET, 2 HDPE, 3 PVC, 4 LDPE, 5 PP, 6 PS, 7 other); pyrolysis, mechanical recycling, biodegradable/bio-based polymers. Green chemistry: CO2-epoxide polycarbonates, lignin-based.

biomolecules.introduction: Biomolecules: carbohydrates, lipids, amino acids/proteins, nucleotides/nucleic acids. Despite huge diversity, built from small monomer alphabets via condensation (dehydration) and broken by hydrolysis. Importance: energy, structure, information, catalysis.

carbohydrates.definition: Polyhydroxy aldehydes/ketones (Cn(H2O)n). Monosaccharides (simple sugars), disaccharides (2 units), polysaccharides (many).

monosaccharides.name: Glucose (aldohexose)
monosaccharides.structure: Open: HOCH2-(CHOH)4-CHO; cyclic: pyranose (6-membered) 99% as α/β-D-glucopyranose (hemiacetal). Aldose.
monosaccharides.stereochem: D-glucose: OH on C5 right in Fischer; α/β anomers at C1; mutarotation equilibrium.
monosaccharides.uses: Blood sugar (5 mM), energy via glycolysis → ATP; polymerizes to starch/cellulose

monosaccharides.name: Fructose (ketohexose)
monosaccharides.structure: Ketohexose, furanose (5-membered) as β-D-fructofuranose; sweetest sugar

monosaccharides.name: Ribose / Deoxyribose
monosaccharides.structure: Aldopentoses; furanose forms in RNA/DNA backbone
monosaccharides.notes: Deoxy = OH at C2 replaced by H

carbohydrates.glycosidicBond: Condensation: -OH (anomeric C) + HO- (another sugar) → O-glycosidic bond + H2O. α vs β matters: α-1,4 (starch, digestible) vs β-1,4 (cellulose, indigestible for humans — needs cellulase). Hydrolysis by glycosidase.

disaccharides.name: Sucrose (table sugar)
disaccharides.structure: α-D-glucose (1→2) β-D-fructose; non-reducing (both anomeric carbons linked)

disaccharides.name: Lactose (milk sugar)
disaccharides.structure: β-D-galactose (1→4) D-glucose; reducing; hydrolyzed by lactase deficiency → lactose intolerance

disaccharides.name: Maltose
disaccharides.structure: α-D-glucose (1→4) D-glucose; product of starch digestion

polysaccharides.name: Starch (amylose + amylopectin)
polysaccharides.structure: α-D-glucose (1→4) chains + occasional α-1,6 branches; amylose helix with I2 → blue-black (iodine test)

polysaccharides.name: Glycogen
polysaccharides.structure: Highly branched α-1,4 with α-1,6 every 8-12 residues; 30k glucoses

polysaccharides.name: Cellulose
polysaccharides.structure: β-1,4 glucose linear; interchain H-bonding + van der Waals → crystalline microfibrils, immense tensile strength

polysaccharides.name: Chitin
polysaccharides.structure: β-1,4 N-acetylglucosamine; second most abundant polymer

carbohydrates.tests: Benedict/Fehling: reducing sugars (free aldehyde) reduce Cu²⁺→Cu2O red ppt; Iodine: starch blue-black; Seliwanoff: ketoses (fructose) red faster than aldoses.

lipids.definition: Non-polar, water-insoluble (hydrophobic) molecules: fats/oils (energy storage), phospholipids (membranes), steroids (signaling).

fattyAcids.name: Saturated
fattyAcids.structure: No C=C; e.g., palmitic C16H32O2 CH3-(CH2)14-COOH (straight, packs well, solid at RT → butter, lard); mp increases with chain length

fattyAcids.name: Unsaturated
fattyAcids.structure: One (mono) or poly (PUFA) cis C=C → kink, poor packing, liquid at RT (oil). Essential: linoleic (C18:2 ω-6), linolenic (C18:3 ω-3) — humans cannot synthesize.
fattyAcids.transFat: Partial hydrogenation gives trans C=C (straight, solid-like) → raises LDL, harmful; banned/reduced

lipids.triglycerides: Glycerol HOCH2-CHOH-CH2OH + 3 fatty acids → triester TAG + 3 H2O (condensation). Stored in adipocytes; energy density 38 kJ/g vs carb 17 kJ/g. Saponification: TAG + 3 NaOH → glycerol + 3 RCOONa (soap); soap amphiphilic (polar head + non-polar tail → micelles). Iodine value = degree of unsaturation.
lipids.phospholipids: Glycerol + 2 fatty acids + phosphate + head group (choline/ethanolamine) → bilayer membrane (hydrophilic head out, hydrophobic tails in). Membrane fluidity: unsaturated ↑ fluidity (kinks); cholesterol regulates.
lipids.steroids: Fused 4-ring (3×6 + 1×5) perhydrocyclopentanophenanthrene: cholesterol (27C, membrane fluidity, precursor to hormones/bile/vitamin D), testosterone, estradiol. Amphipathic but rigid.
lipids.waxes: Long-chain ester + long alcohol → waterproofing (beeswax, cutin).

proteins.definition: Polymers of α-amino acids linked via peptide (amide) bond: NH2-CHR-COOH. 20 standard AAs. Hierarchies: primary (sequence), secondary (α-helix, β-sheet via H-bond), tertiary (overall 3D via hydrophobic, H-bond, disulfide, salt bridges), quaternary (multi-subunit).

aminoAcids.general: H2N-CHR-COOH; at pH 7 mostly zwitterion ⁺H3N-CHR-COO⁻. Stereochemistry: all except Gly chiral, natural = L (S except Cys R). Classification: non-polar (Gly, Ala, Val, Leu, Ile, Met, Pro, Phe, Trp), polar uncharged (Ser, Thr, Cys, Tyr, Asn, Gln), acidic (Asp, Glu, negative), basic (Lys, Arg, His, positive).
aminoAcids.peptideBond: Condensation: –COOH + H2N– → –CO-NH– + H2O. N→C direction. Planar due to resonance (partial double-bond, 40% double). Cis rare (proline ~10%). Hydrolysis by proteases or 6M HCl, 110°C.
aminoAcids.isoelectricPoint: pI = (pKa1+pKa2)/2 for neutral AA; pH where net charge 0; solubility minimum. Polyampholyte.

structure.detail: AA sequence determines all higher structure. Determined via Edman degradation or MS/MS.
α-helix: 3.6 residues/turn, i→i+4 H-bond (C=O···H-N), right-handed, rod (e.g., keratin). β-sheet: strands H-bonded parallel/antiparallel pleated (e.g., silk). Random coil. Ramachandran plot φ/ψ.
structure.stabilized: H-bonds between carbonyl O and amide H

structure.detail: Overall fold via hydrophobic core (non-polar inside), H-bonds, salt bridges (Lys⁺---Asp⁻), disulfides (Cys-S-S-Cys, oxidized). Chaperones assist folding. Denaturation: heat, pH, urea → unfolds; sometimes reversible (Anfinsen).
structure.example: Myoglobin: globular, 153 AAs, 8 helices, heme pocket

structure.detail: Association of subunits: hemoglobin (α2β2, 4 hemes, cooperative O2 binding, allostery); collagen triple helix (Gly-X-Y repeat, X Pro, Y Hyp) → fibers.

proteins.enzymes: Protein catalysts: lower activation energy, specificity (lock-and-key or induced fit), Michaelis-Menten kinetics v = Vmax[S]/(Km+[S]). Cofactors: heme (Fe²⁺ in Hb/cytochrome), NAD⁺/FAD (redox), ATP (energy). Inhibition: competitive (binds active site), non-competitive, irreversible. Optimum pH/T.
proteins.tests: Biuret: Cu²⁺ + peptide → violet (needs ≥2 peptide bonds); Ninhydrin: blue-purple with α-AA (proline yellow); xanthoproteic: nitration of aromatic (yellow).

nucleicAcids.definition: Polymers of nucleotides: phosphate-sugar-base. Information carriers (DNA) and functional (RNA: mRNA, tRNA, rRNA, catalysis).
nucleicAcids.nucleotide: Pentose (ribose in RNA, deoxyribose in DNA 2'-H) + phosphate (PO4³⁻) + nitrogenous base (purine: A,G 2-ring; pyrimidine: C,U/T 1-ring). Link: N-glycosidic bond (sugar C1-N of base) + phosphodiester (C3'-O-P-O-C5' to next sugar). Direction 5'→3'. Base attached to C1', phosphate to C5'.

dna.structure: Double helix (Watson-Crick, 1953): two antiparallel strands, right-handed helix, 10 bp/turn, diameter 2 nm. Sugar-phosphate backbone outside, bases inside H-bonded: A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds). GC richer → higher Tm. Complementarity → replication & transcription.
dna.denaturation: Heating → strands separate (melting, TM where 50% ss). A260 ↑ upon melting (hyperchromicity). Renaturation upon cooling.
dna.packaging: Nucleosomes (DNA wrapped around histone octamer) → chromatin → chromosome.

types: mRNA: codons (3 nt = 1 AA), 5' cap + poly-A tail
tRNA: cloverleaf, anticodon loop, carries AA (acceptor stem)
rna.differences: Single-stranded, U instead of T, ribose 2'-OH makes more labile, versatile catalysis (ribozyme).

nucleicAcids.centralDogma: DNA →(+RNA polymerase) mRNA →(ribosome) protein. Semiconservative replication: each daughter duplex has one parental strand. PCR amplifies DNA via thermal cycling.
nucleicAcids.tests: Diphenylamine (DNA blue), Orcinol (RNA green), UV 260 nm quantification (A260 1 ≈ 50 µg/mL dsDNA). Electrophoresis separates by size.

biomolecules.metabolismOverview: Metabolism: catabolism (breakdown, exergonic: glycolysis, citric acid, oxidative phosphorylation → ATP; β-oxidation of fatty acids) vs anabolism (building, endergonic: gluconeogenesis, protein synthesis). ATP = energy currency (phosphoanhydride ΔG ~ -30 kJ/mol). Coenzymes: NADH/NAD⁺, FADH2/FAD, CoA.
biomolecules.appliedNotes: Isoelectric precipitation (casein pH 4.6); salting out (NH4)2SO4; SDS-PAGE separates proteins by mass; Sanger sequencing / NGS for DNA; biodiesel: transesterification of TAG → FAME (fatty acid methyl esters); hydrogenation of oils → margarine (now avoided).
